newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Sharp outlines roads programme.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Sharp outlines roads programme.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp announced on Monday details of the government's A$1.6 billion roads programme for 1996/97, saying more than a third of that would be spent in the state of New South Wales.

The programme includes pre-construction works, land acquisition and utilities relocation in preparation for a western Sydney orbital road between the south-western suburb of Liverpool and Hornsby in the city's north.

It also included an eastern extension of Melbourne's Western Ring Road, a start on a major rebuilding project for the Eyre Highway across the Nullarbor Plain and tunnels for a new national highway alignment through the Adelaide Hills.
About A$1.0 billion of the total programme funding was allocated to those projects, Sharp said in a statement.
Sharp said the Pacific Highway, between Newcastle and Brisbane, would be reconstructed to a four-lane divided highway, aimed cutting fatalities by about 60 percent.
"The project will cost A$3.0 billion and take 10 years to complete," he said.
Sharp said the roads programme would result in increased economic activity, particularly in rural areas where more than half of the government's funding outlays were targetted.
